newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, French team use laser to find rare metals.
newsitem.headline: Israel, French team use laser to find rare metals.

text.p: Israeli and French researchers have discovered a method of using lasers to identify traces of rare metals in rock formations, Jerusalem's Hebrew University said on Sunday.

Scientists from Hebrew University, the Open University of Israel and France's University of Lyon have developed a method -- laser-excited time-resolved luminescence -- which allows surveyors to locate rare metals, such as uranium, found in minute quantities in apatite rock.
Apatites are sediments consisting of phosphates, calcium and rare metals found as chemical compounds in the rock.

"A laser beamed at apatites cause them to emit various colours. Since each colour can be identified with a specific metal by analysis of the wavelengths and decay time of the emissions, it is possible to get exact information about the metals within the rock," a Hebrew University statement said.
It said the method provides a cost-effective way of determining whether rare metals can be extracted.

"Surveying of land surface areas, even from an airplane, will reveal the presence of rare metals without the need in many cases for costly physical penetration of the rocks and chemical analyses," the statement quoted Hebrew University Professer Renata Reisfeld as saying.
It said laboratory tests of the method had been successful and that it was ready for field trials.
